text:
alex.chen: Heads-up — after the Cilium rollout to west3 last night we’re seeing ~12-18% packet loss between inference GPU pods on the same node / same AZ. Large batched requests to model containers time out. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

maria: yep, saw several 5xx spikes in the dashboards around 02:10 UTC for batch workers. p50/p95 jumped. Noticed retransmits on the pod side when we run perf tests.

raj: I ran a quick tcpdump on host and inside pod. Host capture shows lots of packets with bad checksums but pod-level traffic looks fine. Classic checksum offload illusion. Example from host capture: 

```
16:22:10.123456 IP 10.0.3.12.54321 > 10.0.3.45.9876: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567, ack 1, win 65535, length 222
   (checksum: 0x0000 [unverified])
```

When I disable tx-checksumming on the veth on the host the packet loss numbers drop immediately.

denа: (ops) interesting — last night’s node kernel bumped from 5.15.0-88 -> 5.15.0-101 as part of the OS patch. Also Cilium 1.24.0-rc was pushed to west3 at 01:50. Could be an offload interaction with the NIC driver + eBPF encap.

alex.chen: @tom.ops can you confirm which nodes got the kernel bump + cilium at the same time? We may have a partial rollout hitting edge cases.

tom.ops: checking — rollout was staggered but ~60% of west3 had both updates. Remaining nodes on prior versions. Pinning list: node-a, node-b, node-e.

maria: quick iperf3 between two impacted pods (inside same node) before/after disabling checksum offload:
```
# on pod A
iperf3 -c 10.0.3.45 -t 8 -J
# observed: high retransmits, throughput drops ~30%
```

raj: steps I ran to reproduce and mitigate:
1) SSH to host -> `ip link set dev vethXYZ tx off` 
2) k8s exec -> re-run workload; failure rate drops to baseline

So seems like the host-side offload + encapsulation (vxlan/geneve) with eBPF encapsulation keys is causing wrong checksum visibility on host capture and actual clobbering in flight.

platform-oncall: this matches a behavior we saw in lab with vendor NIC firmware 2.1.4 + kernel 5.15.0-100 where GSO + tunnel offload produced packet corruption for TCP segments > MSS.

dena: can we triage with a quick rollback of the Cilium update on a small subset? If the kernel bump alone causes it we need to rollback nodes instead but prefer to roll back Cilium first (faster).

alex.chen: Agree. Proposal: rollback cilium on node-a/node-b (two canaries) and repro. If fixed -> schedule full rollback for west3 and open a vendor ticket for NIC driver/kernel combo.

maria: I can do the canary rollback now. patch: `helm upgrade --reuse-values --set image.tag=1.23.8 cilium cilium/cilium`

sre-bot: Deploy started by maria — cilium rollback to 1.23.8 on nodes [node-a, node-b]. CI tests in progress.

maria: rollback complete on node-a/node-b. Re-ran the same batch load — error rate down to normal, no extra retransmits on pod-level tcpdump. Looks promising.

raj: confirmed. Host tcpdump no longer shows corrupted checksums, iperf3 recovered throughput.

tom.ops: rolling a wider rollback across remaining west3 nodes now. Also opening a runbook note: "Cilium encap offload interaction — rollback to last known-good (1.23.8) until vendor patch".

platform-oncall: opened ticket with NIC vendor + kernel folks. Attaching preliminary logs and sample pcap. Attn: fw 2.1.4 + kernel 5.15.0-101 + Cilium encap path triggers truncated GSO segments.

alex.chen: Thanks all. Action items:
- Rollback complete across west3 (in progress) — @tom.ops to confirm when finished
- Vendor ticket + lab repro with exact firmware/kernel/cilium combo — @platform-oncall
- Add a quick health-check in rollout CI to run small pod-to-pod large-packet iperf test before promoting Cilium in prod — @dena

maria: once rollback finishes I’ll draft a postmortem note and put tentative outage window if vendor confirms patch needed.

alex.chen: Nice quick turnaround. Marking channel for follow-up: if rollback doesn't clear it fully we will also test node kernel rollback. :thumbsup:
